scheme_name: Construction of Dudhghar/ Godown (Scheduled Tribe Area)
description:
The Construction of Dudhghar/Godown scheme is a welfare initiative launched by the Government of India to support Scheduled Tribes in rural areas.

This scheme was introduced in the year 2019 under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

The primary objective of the scheme is to enhance the livelihood opportunities for Scheduled Tribe communities by providing them with infrastructure for the storage of milk and dairy products.

The scheme aims to construct Dudhghars or godowns in various tribal areas across the country.

These facilities are designed to improve the collection and storage of milk, thereby ensuring better prices for dairy farmers.

The government has set a target to construct at least 1,000 Dudhghars across different states by the end of the financial year 2024.

Each Dudhghar is expected to have a storage capacity of approximately 5,000 liters of milk.

The estimated cost for constructing a single Dudhghar is around INR 25 lakhs.

The scheme provides financial assistance of up to 90% of the total project cost for the construction of these facilities.

The remaining 10% is expected to be contributed by the implementing agency or local cooperative societies.

Eligible beneficiaries under this scheme are primarily members of Scheduled Tribes.

The age limit for beneficiaries is set at a minimum of 18 years.

There are no specific educational qualifications required to apply for this scheme.

However, applicants must be engaged in dairy farming or related activities.

The income criteria for eligibility is that the annual income of the applicant should not exceed INR 2.5 lakhs.

The application process involves several steps.

Interested beneficiaries must first approach the local Tribal Welfare Department.

They need to fill out an application form which can be obtained from the department's office or their official website.

The application form requires details such as the applicant's name, address, age, income, and details of dairy farming activities.

Along with the application form, applicants must submit identity proof such as an Aadhar card or voter ID.

They must also provide proof of income which can be in the form of an income certificate issued by the local revenue authority.

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local Tribal Welfare Department.

The department will assess the viability of the project and the applicant's eligibility.

If approved, the project proposal will be forwarded to the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for final approval.

Upon receiving approval from the Ministry, the funds will be released to the implementing agency.

The timeline for the entire application process can vary but typically takes around 3 to 6 months.

Disbursement of funds is usually done in installments based on the progress of construction.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project.

Subsequent installments are released based on the completion of predefined milestones.

The implementing authorities for this scheme include the Ministry of Tribal Affairs at the central level.

At the state level, the Tribal Welfare Department is responsible for the implementation.

Each state has its own designated nodal officer to oversee the scheme's execution.

Beneficiaries can contact the local Tribal Welfare Department for any queries or assistance.

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to uplift the socio-economic status of Scheduled Tribes in India.

According to the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes constitute about 8.6% of India's total population.

This demographic represents over 104 million individuals across the country.

The government recognizes the potential of dairy farming as a sustainable livelihood option for these communities.

By providing infrastructure such as Dudhghars, the scheme aims to reduce post-harvest losses.

It also seeks to enhance the income of tribal farmers by ensuring better storage and marketing of milk.

The construction of these facilities is expected to create local employment opportunities.

It will also encourage cooperative societies among tribal communities.

The scheme aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

It aims to promote self-sufficiency among tribal communities in dairy production.

The initiative is also expected to improve the nutritional status of tribal populations.

By increasing the availability of dairy products, the scheme contributes to better health outcomes.

The government has allocated a budget of INR 250 crores for the implementation of this scheme over the next five years.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme will be conducted regularly to assess its impact.

The Ministry of Tribal Affairs will publish annual reports detailing the progress of the scheme.

These reports will include information on the number of Dudhghars constructed and the beneficiaries served.

The scheme is expected to foster greater participation of women in dairy farming.

Women in tribal areas often play a crucial role in managing dairy activities.

By empowering them through this scheme, the government aims to promote gender equality.

The Dudhghar facilities will also serve as training centers for dairy farming techniques.

Workshops will be organized to educate beneficiaries about best practices in dairy management.

The scheme encourages the use of modern technology in dairy farming.

This includes the adoption of improved breeds of cattle and better feeding practices.

The government aims to create a sustainable dairy ecosystem in tribal regions.

The initiative is part of a larger framework of welfare schemes focused on tribal development.

These include schemes for education, health, and skill development.

The Construction of Dudhghar/Godown scheme is a significant step towards holistic development.

It addresses multiple facets of tribal life including economic, social, and nutritional aspects.

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of this scheme reach the intended beneficiaries.

Regular feedback will be collected from beneficiaries to improve the scheme's implementation.

The success of the scheme will depend on the active participation of tribal communities.

By working together with local cooperatives, the government aims to create a sustainable model for dairy farming.

This initiative is a testament to the government's commitment to uplift marginalized communities in India.
